text: A sommelier tilts a bottle toward the lamplight, reads the label aloud in Old Corellian, sets it down with a slight bow.
Ozone and rosewood. A privacy emitter at every other booth, all of them lit.
Strings playing too softly to follow. Conversation pitched to match.
Every privacy field in the room drops at once. Three seconds. Then they come back.
A server lights a dessert tableside. Blue flame, no smoke. Half the room watches.
The lift chimes. Two heads at the bar turn, then return to their drinks at exactly the same speed.
Imperial dress greys at the corner banquette. The room is louder than it needs to be.
A coaster slides over a credit chit at the bar. Neither hand acknowledges the other.
The music cuts. One full beat of silence. Then it resumes, a different piece, slightly slower.
Bantha-leather banquettes the color of dried wine. Someone laughs once, briefly, and stops.
The maître d' walks the room every twelve minutes. Nothing visibly changes when he passes.
A senator-district staffer enters, scans the room, leaves without speaking. The maître d' notes something on a flimsi.
His glass is full. It's been full since the players walked in. He's watching the lift, not the door.
An Imperial officer in dress greys nurses a single brandy, posture immaculate. Switches to formal High Galactic when addressed — and doesn't notice he does it.
A Twi'lek woman in pearl-grey sits alone at a four-top. Adjusts other people's cuffs when they walk past her booth, without asking. They thank her.
'Compliments of a guest who prefers not to be named.' The sommelier sets the bottle down at the players' table and waits.
Piercing eyes, a duelling scar at the jaw, the wrong kind of stillness for a private brandy. Repeats the last word of every sentence in a whisper, then denies it.
An older Chagrian holds his glass by the rim, never the body. Refers to the Emperor only as 'the current administration.' Will not be drawn further.
Has been signing flimsis for an hour, one at a time, sliding each into a different pocket. Pauses half a beat before any reply.
A human woman with grey at the temples, soldier's spine under a black evening dress. Scans every entrance on a count of three.
A Kel Dor in muted formal robes raises a finger; the sommelier arrives. He asks three different ways whether the players are expected. Each more polite than the last.
A Bothan in a half-cape watches the lift doors, datapad face-down on the table. Sniffs the air mid-sentence then turns sharply, every time.
Crosses the room toward the players smiling, gets their names slightly wrong, kisses the air beside each cheek. Has never met them before.
A Mirialan in a House Organa retainer's sash. Treats every mention of the Jedi as a small social error and graciously moves past it.
A woman at the bar laughs at something on her datapad, looks up at the players, laughs again. Compliments their clothing in a way that feels like inventory.
A Sullustan in a tailor's measured silence. Will not look directly at any human; tracks them in the bar mirror.
A young Zabrak duelist removes her gloves one finger at a time, watching the players. Hums between sentences — same three-note phrase, every time.
An elderly Ithorian sips slowly, eyes closed. Has been here when each shift started.
A human in a charcoal jacket reads a flimsi pamphlet at the bar, drink untouched.
A bartender pours three measures in a single uninterrupted arc, eyes never leaving the customer.
A protocol droid in club livery stands at parade rest beside the coat check, idle for the moment.
A server polishes a glass at the side station, holding it up to the light between passes.
A red-eyed human sits alone with two empties and a third half-finished. Quiet, not maudlin.
A hostess at the lectern updates the reservations console, lips moving silently as she counts.
A bored Duros at the end of the bar flicks credit chits one at a time into an empty glass.
Two human women at a side booth, ages thirty years apart, identical mannerisms. They trade the same brief glance every time someone passes their table.
Two Imperial officers in civilian black are arguing in whispers. One finishes the other's sentences after a deliberate half-beat permission pause.
A Pantoran in formalwear and his Falleen companion. They never speak. They mirror each other's drinks down to the angle of the glass.
A senator-district staffer and a journalist with a tucked recorder are not making eye contact. He talks; she listens; neither drinks.
Two human investors compare datapads quietly, nodding in unison at things only they understand.
An older couple at the window-table, hands resting near each other but not touching, watching the skylane lights.
Two off-duty club servers at the back stairwell share a single tea, swapping the cup back and forth.
A Twi'lek couple deep in conversation, glasses untouched. He laughs softly at something she didn't mean as a joke.
Two human businesswomen split a single dessert with two spoons, one of them taking notes between bites.
Four young aristocrats at a round table go silent in perfect unison whenever a server approaches. Resume mid-sentence the moment the server leaves.
A table of corporate accountants in matching dark suits, laughing at someone's quiet joke. Three glasses, four people; one isn't drinking.
Five university friends crowd a corner booth, toasting something none of them will explain to the servers.
A retirement party at the long table — three older humans, a Sullustan, gentle laughter, one chair empty with a glass at the place setting.
A grey-haired human in COMPNOR pins crosses the room toward the players, smiling. Three steps in, he stops, frowns at a chrono, turns back.
A Mon Calamari in House Organa colors sits with a single glass of water. Cannot perceive sarcasm. Will answer rhetorical questions with great care.
Has paid the bill three times in the last hour, each time waving the server away. Taps the table in groups of three between thoughts.
A senator at the next table mentions one of the players by name to her companion, then changes the subject.
The sommelier presents a bottle the players did not order. A folded flimsi is tied to the neck with silver wire.
A junior staffer at the bar accidentally meets a player's eyes, blanches, looks away too fast. He keeps adjusting his collar.
A small folded card appears under one player's glass between sip and sip. No one is at the next table.
The maître d' approaches and asks, with perfect courtesy, whether the gentleman who reserved the players' table will be joining them.
A protocol droid in club livery requests, politely, that the players accompany it to a private room. It will not say at whose request.
The privacy emitter at the players' booth fails with a soft pop. Three nearby tables conspicuously do not look over.
Two patrons at the next stools stand and leave their drinks unfinished. The Zabrak duelist at the bar is removing her gloves.
Three Imperial naval officers in dress uniforms have just entered, and the maître d' is leading them directly toward the players' booth.
Every server in the room steps simultaneously to the walls. The lift behind the players opens. Two figures in ISB charcoal are already inside.
The Bothan with the face-down datapad stands, walks to the players' booth, sets the datapad in front of them and keeps walking toward the lift.
The duelist's gloves are off, she's three meters from the players' table, and the sommelier has stopped pouring mid-glass.
